In mammalian cells, the signaling molecules are free fatty acids (FFA) and oxidized derivatives of polyunsaturated fatty, which
are transported in and out of the cell with the help of a membrane protein, the fatty acid transporter (FAT). FFA is taken up by
a speciﬁc fatty acid binding protein (FABP) and has various metabolic fates in the cytoplasm (Fig. 2).
